key_insight: The paper shows that strong agent execution can still leave product decisions unresolved, so decision auditing must focus on what users would value, not just what the agent did.
engineering_relevance: For AI systems, preserving structured decision context and source-labeled inputs can reduce unnecessary uncertainty when auditing model-driven product choices.
method: Defines a decision-specific audit using declared observation channels and value contrasts.
Maps each audit to compatible intervals and witness populations from identification and decision theory.
Implements an offline workflow with a source-labeled decision receipt and viewer for inspection.
evidence_signal: In a frozen experiment, 4,800 requests across two pinned model snapshots left all 36 conservative primary intervals unresolved, while an exploratory follow-up and deterministic extraction resolved some comparisons.
watch_item: Unresolved intervals can reflect structural ambiguity or weak identification, so more telemetry does not always fix the audit without better decision-relevant inputs.
paper_title: The Delegation Blind Spot: Auditing Product Decisions from Agent Choices
